title: introduce-cost-rules-engine-and-autotune-batching-defaults
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Summary: Add a Cost Rules Engine that automatically recommends and applies batching and KV-cache defaults per model and workload profile, exposes quantization profile hints for safe auto-application, and introduces a unit-economics estimator in the console and CLI. Motivation: customers routinely ask for hands-off cost tuning; operational teams want reproducible, audited defaults that reduce per-token costs without surprising latency regressions. This PR bundles runtime heuristics, a small rules DSL, console UI plumbing, and an opt-in rollout for auto-quantization. What changed (high level): - new runtime module redwood/serving/cost_rules.py with rules evaluation, telemetry hooks, and safe-apply gates - batcher tuning extension that selects default batch sizes based on latency SLOs and sequence-length histograms - KV cache policy defaults and prefix cache eligibility heuristics - quantization profiling pipeline (offline profiler + runtime hinting) and a safe auto-apply policy with rollback - console/CLI cost estimator showing projected per-token unit economics with suggested knobs - integration tests, docs, and an opt-in feature flag + audit logs Rollout plan: default rules are disabled by default for existing tenants. We enable the rules engine for internal canaries and add a gradual opt-in toggle in the console. Quantization auto-apply is gated behind a policy that requires: a) offline eval against golden prompt set, b) latency/regression guardrails, and c) explicit tenant opt-in. Checklist: - [x] implement rule evaluator and runtime hooks - [x] expose console estimator and API endpoints - [x] add offline quant profile pipeline and safe-apply path - [x] add unit + integration tests - [x] add docs and release notes - [x] add audit events and rollout flag Notes on safety: the rules engine never mutates a serving model binary directly; it returns a recommended configuration which a controlled subsystem applies with canarying and audits. The PR includes a conservative default profile that favors latency SLOs for small-sequence chat workloads and cost for high-throughput embedding workloads. Related: ENG-3412 (cost-automation epic), ENG-3470 (quantization-safety), SUP-1298 (customer support case motivating default cache rules).

review_conversation: Ava Chen: High level LGTM. Please ensure telemetry includes pre/post token-cost breakdown and include schema for audit events.
Priya Kapoor: Added observability proto and wired pre/post token metrics. See redwood/observability/events/cost_rules_audit.proto.

Miguel Santos: Concern: automatic quantization risks subtle quality regressions for instruction-following models. Suggest conservative rollout and a required eval pass. Also call out per-tenant opt-in in docs.
Priya Kapoor: Agree. Implemented safe-apply policy (requires offline eval pass and rollback hook). Added docs and feature flag page. Quant auto-apply disabled by default.
Liam O'Connor: Noted a potential race in batcher config writes during scale events. Suggested a lock around update path. I added a mutex in tuner.go and a unit test replicating scale churn.
Ava Chen: CI failure was a real flake in integration test; reran and now all checks passed. Approving to merge once CI green.
Miguel Santos: Approve. Leaving a suggestion for a follow-up to tune embedding-heavy workloads after 2-week telemetry window.
release_notes: Add a Cost Rules Engine that recommends batching and cache defaults, an opt-in quantization safe-apply pipeline, and a unit-economics estimator in the console/CLI. Disabled by default for existing tenants; expected to reduce per-token cost by up to ~20% for high-throughput embedding workloads when enabled. See redwood/docs/cost-rules.md for configuration and rollout guidance.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag in helm: costRules.enabled=true for internal canaries. Monitor metrics: cost_rules.recommendation.applied_count, cost_rules.rollback_count, tokens.per_second and request.latency.p50/p95. Keep quant auto-apply disabled until 1-week canary telemetry looks stable.
